bib.title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation

read.skipped: reference list skimmed; figures are images and were not read

question: How can a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model be personalized from 3-5 images of a subject so it renders that subject in new contexts?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning all layers on few images with a rare-token identifier plus class noun, and a self-generated class prior preservation loss, binds the subject without language drift or overfitting.
contributions: A technique to embed a subject in a text-to-image diffusion model via a rare-token identifier and fine-tuning
An autogenous class-specific prior preservation loss against language drift and low diversity
A new dataset of 30 subjects and an evaluation protocol with subject fidelity (DINO, CLIP-I) and prompt fidelity (CLIP-T) metrics
Applications: recontextualization, art rendition, novel view synthesis, property modification

method.summary: Fine-tune a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model (Imagen, or Stable Diffusion) on 3-5 images captioned 'a [V] [class noun]' with the standard denoising loss plus a prior-preservation term on images the frozen model generated for 'a [class noun]'. For Imagen the 64->256 SR model is also fine-tuned.

datasets.name: DreamBooth dataset
datasets.size: 30 subjects (21 objects, 9 live subjects/pets), 25 prompts (objects: 20 recontextualization + 5 property modification; live: 10 recontextualization, 10 accessorization, 5 property modification)
datasets.split: 3-5 images per subject for fine-tuning; 4 generated images per subject per prompt = 3,000 images
datasets.source: collected by authors or from Unsplash; released on project page

datasets.name: Class prior samples
datasets.size: ~1000 'a [class noun]' samples generated by the frozen model (fewer can be used)
datasets.source: ancestral sampler on frozen pretrained model

models.name: Imagen
models.architecture: cascaded diffusion: 64x64 base, SR 64->256, SR 256->1024; T5-XXL text encoder, SentencePiece tokenizer
models.init_from: pretrained Imagen (provided by Google Brain authors)

other.rare_token_rule: uniform random tokens of 3 or fewer Unicode characters, T5-XXL token range 5000-10000

models.name: Stable Diffusion
models.architecture: latent diffusion; U-Net (and possibly text encoder) trained, decoder fixed

training.objective: squared-error x-prediction denoising loss (Eq 1) plus lambda-weighted prior-preservation term on self-generated class samples (Eq 2)
training.hardware: one TPUv4 (Imagen); one NVIDIA A100 (Stable Diffusion)

other.layers_tuned: all layers incl. text-conditioned ones for max fidelity
other.SR_finetune: 64->256 SR essential for most subjects; 256->1024 helps some
other.SR_noise_augmentation: reduced from 1e-3 to 1e-5 for 256 SR fine-tune

inference.decoding: ancestral sampler (class sample generation); DDIM or ancestral sampler at inference per supp
inference.samples: 4 images per subject per prompt; 3,000 total
inference.prompting: 'a [V] [class noun] [context]'; art: 'a painting of a [V] [class noun] in the style of [painter]'; property: 'a cross of a [V] dog and a [target species]'; accessories: 'a [V] [class noun] wearing [accessory]'

metrics.name: DINO
metrics.definition: average pairwise cosine similarity between ViT-S/16 DINO embeddings of generated and real images (preferred subject fidelity metric)

metrics.name: CLIP-I
metrics.definition: average pairwise cosine similarity between CLIP embeddings of generated and real images

metrics.name: CLIP-T
metrics.definition: average cosine similarity between prompt and image CLIP embeddings

metrics.name: PRES
metrics.definition: average pairwise DINO similarity between generated images of random subjects of the prior class and real images of the specific subject; higher means prior collapse

metrics.name: DIV
metrics.definition: average LPIPS cosine similarity between generated images of same subject and prompt (paper's wording)

metrics.name: User preference
metrics.definition: pairwise choice vs Textual Inversion with a Cannot Determine option, majority vote; 72 users x 25 questions, 3 users per questionnaire

baselines: Textual Inversion (Gal et al.) on Stable Diffusion, with its published hyperparameters
DALL-E 2 and Imagen with prompt engineering (qualitative)
eval.protocol: Ablations: PPL on 15 subjects (Imagen); class noun on 5 subjects (Imagen); input-image count on 2 subjects. No seeds or significance tests stated beyond a Pearson p-value for metric/human correlation.

availability.code: not stated in text (project page https://dreambooth.github.io/)
availability.data: dataset and evaluation protocol on the project webpage

limits: Failure modes: wrong context for rare prompts, context-appearance entanglement, overfitting when prompt resembles training setting (Fig 9)
Some subjects (dogs, cats) are easier than rare ones; hallucinated subject features possible
Optimizer, batch size, schedule, Stable Diffusion version and seeds are not stated
Only one comparable baseline (Textual Inversion), compared on SD only; user study covers SD only
Societal impact: could be used to mislead viewers

terms.definition: the model slowly forgets how to generate subjects of the same class as the target subject
prior preservation metric: average pairwise DINO similarity between random class generations and real images of the subject

lineage.work: Stable Diffusion / latent diffusion (Rombach et al.)
